title: Rigveda 10.154: To the departed
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.154: To the departed: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.154 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to the dead one. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 137r-137v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.154.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 137r
translation.original_text:
1soma̱ eke̍bhyaḥ pavate ghṛ̱tam eka̱ upā̍sate | yebhyo̱ madhu̍ pra̱dhāva̍ti̱ tām̐ś ci̍d e̱vāpi̍ gacchatāt ||
2tapa̍sā̱ ye a̍nādhṛ̱ṣyās tapa̍sā̱ ye sva̍r ya̱yuḥ | tapo̱ ye ca̍kri̱re maha̱s tām̐ś ci̍d e̱vāpi̍ gacchatāt ||
3ye yudhya̍nte pra̱dhane̍ṣu̱ śūrā̍so̱ ye ta̍nū̱tyaja̍ḥ | ye vā̍ sa̱hasra̍dakṣiṇā̱s tām̐ś ci̍d e̱vāpi̍ gacchatāt ||
translation.text:
1FOR some is Soma purified, some sit by sacrificial oil: To those for whom the meath flows forth, even to those let him depart.
2Invincible through Fervour, those whom Fervour hath advanced to heaven, Who showed great Fervour in their lives, -even to those let him depart.
3The heroes who contend in war and boldly cast their lives away, Or who give guerdon thousandfold, -even to those let him depart.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 137r (OPenn image 136, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.153.3 ‹tvam indrāsi vṛtrahā vy›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 137v, begins in RV 10.154.4 ‹pitṝn tapasvato yama tām̐ś›. Verses 10.154.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.154.4-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 137v
translation.original_text:
4ye ci̱t pūrva̍ ṛta̱sāpa̍ ṛ̱tāvā̍na ṛtā̱vṛdha̍ḥ | pi̱tṝn tapa̍svato yama̱ tām̐ś ci̍d e̱vāpi̍ gacchatāt ||
5sa̱hasra̍ṇīthāḥ ka̱vayo̱ ye go̍pā̱yanti̱ sūrya̍m | ṛṣī̱n tapa̍svato yama tapo̱jām̐ api̍ gacchatāt ||
translation.text:
4Yea, the first followers of Law, Law's pure and holy strengtheners, The Fathers, Yama! Fervour-moved,even to those let him depart.
5Skilled in a thousand ways and means, the sages who protect the Sun, The R̥ishis, Yama! Fervour-moved,– even to those let him depart.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 137v (OPenn image 137, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.154.4 ‹pitṝn tapasvato yama tām̐ś›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 138r, begins in RV 10.155.4 ‹-budbudayāśavaḥ›. Verses 10.154.4-5 end on this page; 10.154.4 begins on fol. 137r.
